title: Orthodromic AV reentrant tachycardia (AVRT)
summary: The impulse goes down the AV node, up an accessory pathway to the atrium and round again.

events.label: Sinus beat
events.caption: A normal sinus beat. This accessory pathway only conducts backwards (a concealed pathway), so the beat looks normal and there is no delta wave.
events.ecg: A normal P wave, PR interval and narrow QRS.

events.label: Premature atrial beat
events.caption: A premature atrial beat starts early, before the circuit has recovered. This is how the tachycardia begins.

events.label: Slowed in the AV node
events.caption: The accessory pathway cannot conduct forwards, so the early impulse can only go down the AV node. Arriving soon after its last use, the node conducts it slowly.
events.ecg: The PR interval is longer than normal.

events.label: Ventricles
events.caption: The ventricles activate through the normal conduction system.

events.label: Back up the pathway
events.caption: The impulse now finds the accessory pathway and conducts backwards to the atrium. The atria and ventricles have been activated in series, which can start a circuit.
events.ecg: A retrograde P wave follows just after the QRS.

events.label: Circuit established
events.caption: The atria are activated from the pathway end, the left lateral wall first, and the impulse re-enters the AV node. It goes round: down the AV node, up the accessory pathway, across the atria.
events.ecg: Each lap gives a QRS and a retrograde P wave soon after it.

events.label: Tachycardia
events.caption: A regular narrow-complex tachycardia at about 200 per minute. Because the ventricles are activated through the normal system, the QRS stays narrow.

teaching_points: Orthodromic AVRT: antegrade conduction down the AV node, retrograde up an accessory pathway; the QRS is narrow (slide 65).
Initiation: a premature atrial (or ventricular) beat meets unidirectional block and finds the circuit ready (slides 50, 64).
The accessory pathway is the usual ablation target; the AV node can also be slowed with drugs or a vagal manoeuvre.
